why: Six tiny grants (median $1k, FY2025) for depression screening and student risk assessments at two Minnesota schools; related but small.
A single $11k suicide prevention grant to a high school (FY2025): on topic but too little evidence.
Most of its 18 grants (FY2025) are for suicide counseling support, plus suicide prevention awareness and clinical therapist support.
Pays young adults' mental-health expenses to reduce suicide, but the money goes to private counseling practices (several LLC/PLLC), not nonprofit programs.
Grants through FY2025 for suicide prevention, including AFSP, treatment access for young adults and Hope for the Day's high school program.
Recurring Ohio grants for suicide prevention, school-based interventions and counselors (8 each), latest FY2024.
Recent grants (FY2025) for suicide prevention programs, including AFSP, plus mental-health patient assistance.
Ten grants (FY2023) for suicide and drug prevention education, but they go only to Oregon school districts and high schools.
Behavioral-health mini-grants focused on substance use and overdose prevention (plus one mobile crisis unit and one youth project), not teen suicide prevention.
Large grants (FY2024) to the Suicide Prevention Coalition of Eagle Valley and Hope Center, plus 24/7 crisis co-response including school-based services.
